newsitem.title: UK: Softs outlook--sugar seen firm, coffee holds.
newsitem.headline: Softs outlook--sugar seen firm, coffee holds.

text.p: The London white sugar market could draw some support this week from the current seasonal dip in European supply while coffee may meander in tight ranges amid the summer lull.

Cocoa's swing will be dictated by New York's equivalent market and currency gyrations. Technically, cocoa's upward progress looked promising if it managed to steer clear of the key 1,000 stg support on September and 1,035 on December, traders said.
In white sugar, traders said spot October would remain well supported before new European crops came on line as August is traditionally seen as a period of tight physical supply for quality whites.
"There's a lot of argument saying if there's any bullish news to come out, most of will be led by the whites," said one trader.
Demand for whites could come from Indonesia if raws prices stay high, he added.
Market sources said fund players in London were content to wait for another burst of bullish sentiment before returning to the market as they had already increased their long positions.
"They've still got the capacity to buy some more but the whole thing is just going to meander around," the trader said.
"There aren't many fund stops around on the upside because the funds have got their long positions in and they're not bothered," said another trader, noting October sell-stops at $323 and below.
Traders said interest on the London spreads was likely to be centred on October/March, avoiding the second-month December contract.
The position traditionally attracts relatively little interest as there is no equivalent position in New York for arbitrage trading.
Robusta coffee futures, pausing to consolidate recent gains, are likely to trade sideways with September holding at the key $1,600 support basis September. A key chart hurdle is pegged at $1,700.
But analysts said upward movement could be a struggle and the market could be content with current dull and familiar range-bound trade.
One factor that could spice the market up is frost news in Brazil. A frost scare last week sparked a brief rally in New York arabica futures.

Weather forecaster Cropcast said on Friday long-range guidance models showed the greatest threat of cold weather reaching Brazil's coffee belt will be toward the middle of next week, with the probability of a freeze 20 percent.

However forecaster Weather Services Corp said that while somewhat cooler temperatures could reach Brazil's coffee belt during the second half of the week, high pressure expected to build in Argentina this week is likely to pass well south of coffee growing areas.
Brazil's coffee districts have so far escaped damaging frost this year. The last severe frosts were in 1994.
In cocoa, LIFFE's September contract seemed to have pushed quite well above the 1,000 stg support after the recent spike down to 965.
The market, building a stronger base, could clear the double top at 1,028 before making further headway towards the ultimate upside objective at 1,060.
"Technicals are quite positive but fundamentally there's not much to get excited about," said one trader.
Players were awaiting a fuller picture on the size of the coming Ivorian main crop. Even the size of the mid-crop remained uncertain. --London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
